title: Three Months and One Short Form
subtitle: 经济消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：loan　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 loan 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1992 the clerk ① took the loan that no trader in the bank would have recorded, and he said the taking was the whole of the month. The ② loan, meaning the credit itself and not the form, ran three months and stayed unrecorded in the book; a loan, he said, is the only thing in a bank that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ loan in that bank had the same short form beside it, and the ④ loan at the far counter, meaning the sum they kept for the children to repay and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A loan, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the clerk said the recording is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the loan was the whole of the matter, meaning the trust and not the credit. The ⑥ loan, meaning the trust and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; loan, he said, is either something you take or the only word that means both a credit and a trust. He said the trust is the part they remember.

By 1997 the ⑦ loan had become a line in a statement, and the statement had become an argument about the short form. The ⑧ loan of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in August, was one bank and three months of recording; loan, he said, is either the sum at the far counter or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ loan I remember is the credit recorded in the statement, which closed in 1999 and is still recorded as the quietest in the bank. A ⑩ loan, my mother said in 2001, is the only credit that improves by being recorded; every loan, she said, is a trust that has agreed to look like a credit. She said the trust was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 贷款；借款（指银行里每一笔旁边的那一笔）
B. n. 贷款；借款（指那笔借款本身，与表格相对）
C. 固定搭配：take the loan 借这笔贷款
D. n. 贷款；借款（指留给孩子们还的那一笔那一笔）
E. n. 借贷之事（抽象总称，指一处银行的贷款之事）
F. n. 贷款；借款（指对账单里写到、被记载的的那一笔）
G. n. 信用、承诺（指一件事里人人都还却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 承诺（抽象总称，指人人都还却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: take the loan 意为“借这笔贷款”，1992 年那位柜员把银行里没有一位摊主肯记载的一笔贷款做了一遍。
loan 意为“贷款；借款”，指那笔借款本身而不是表格，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被记载。
loan 意为“贷款；借款”，指银行里每一笔旁边的那一笔，每一笔旁边都有同一张薄薄的表格。
loan 意为“贷款；借款”，指最远那张柜台留给孩子们还的那一笔那一笔，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
loan 意为“信用、承诺”，指一件事里人人都还却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份信用就是那件事的全部。
loan 意为“承诺”，指人人都还却无人提起的那样东西而不是那笔借款，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
loan 意为“贷款；借款”，指对账单里写到、被记载的的那一笔，到 1997 年这一笔成了对账单里的一行。
loan 意为“借贷之事”，柜员八月写道，整件事的贷款之事是一处银行和三个月份的记载。
loan 意为“贷款；借款”，我记得的是对账单里记载过的那一笔，1999 年还清了，至今仍被说成银行里最安静的一笔。
loan 为抽象总称，母亲 2001 年说，贷款是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的借款。
